name: libhttp
listed_description: A cross-platform HTTP and HTTPS library in C/C++.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README (MIT, about 1,000 stars, fork of Civetweb/Mongoose, not archived) has feature lists and no benchmark or speed claim; issue #42 'Benchmarks?' (2017, closed) asks for benchmarks and has no reply with numbers; issue #41 'Why?' is unanswered; the project site libhttp.org is not reachable here. Web searches found no third-party shootout that includes it, and the framework shootouts opened (nanoant/WebFrameworkBenchmark, liu-rui/webframeworkbenchmark) list libmicrohttpd, Kore and Onion but not libhttp or Civetweb.

name: libhttpd
listed_description: Library to add basic web server capabilities to an application (Hughes Technologies).
reason: Directional only. The project pages (hughes.com.au, hughestech.com.au) are EGRESS_BLOCKED here; search excerpts say only that the library has 'very low overheads' with no numbers or baseline, and no third-party benchmark naming libhttpd was found.

name: libhttpserver
listed_description: C++ library for creating an embedded Rest HTTP server (and more).
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. README (LGPL-2.1, 953 stars, wrapper over libmicrohttpd) calls itself high-performance and lists tuning options (turbo, TCP_FASTOPEN, suppress_date_header) and three examples/benchmark_*.cpp micro-benchmark servers, but no result numbers; ChangeLog 0.17.5 says 'saving ~15% on average per request' from URL normalisation (self-comparison), PR #365 lists optimisations with no numbers, issue #169 is a bug report (26,716 req/s without httperf rate limiting) with no baseline, and DR-005 only says allocation savings matter above 10k resp/s. TechEmpower FrameworkBenchmarks has a frameworks/C++/libhttpserver plaintext entry (archived 2026-03-24), but techempower.com results are blocked here, so no number could be read; lead for a later pass with wider network access.

name: libjson-rpc-cpp
listed_description: JSON-RPC framework for C++ servers and clients.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README (MIT, 986 stars) is about features, the stub generator and JSON-RPC 2.0 compatibility with no benchmark or speed claim; the only performance-related issues (#170 poll/epoll by default, #96 async client) carry no numbers against another library; web search found no benchmark against gRPC or any other RPC framework.
